# Exposed simplex-face atomic plateaus: actual descent and a closed-minor obstruction

This is an unpenalized, exact compatible deformation theorem. It extends
the exposed-vertex-only plateau descent to nonvertex bases in exposed
simplex faces, in particular to arbitrary boundary edges of a planar base.
It does not assume that a closed minor can be shrunk independently, and
an actual three-fiber calibration shows why that replacement would be false.

The buffered depth is the affine-invariant positive-affine-multiplier
version, with M, covariance Sigma and energy all updated with the body.
The geometric-mean normalization of the positive affine multiplier ell is
retained. No extra penalty functional is included or dropped.

## 1. Actual hypotheses and statement

Let P=conv(P) intersect Lambda be finite and lattice-complete, with k
occupied parities. Let positive compatible convex fibers K_z of continuous
dimension d>=1 have volumes V_z and total M. Write B=conv(P). Fix epsilon>0
and a positive affine ell with

    sum_z (V_z/M) log ell(z)=0.

Let Q>0 be the actual global raw buffered maximum, and I its set of
maximizing integer bases. For p in P, write F_p for its minimal face in B.
The full polytope B is allowed as a minimal face. Assume:

(A) EVERY p in I is pure-base-bound and its atomic depth is paid by its
    whole minimal face:

       b_base(p)=sum_(z in P intersect F_p) V_z=Q.              (1)

(B) Every distinct face F_p occurring for p in I is a simplex.

(C) The level is bad for the unpenalized target:

       Q/M<Gamma_d/k,       Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.                (2)

Then there is an actual positive compatible family, arbitrarily close to
the original one, and a continuously renormalized positive affine ell_t,
whose normalized global buffered maximum is STRICTLY smaller than Q/M.
Consequently a joint unpenalized bad minimum cannot satisfy (A)--(B).

The shape of each fiber is arbitrary. No common fiber normals, centroids,
central symmetry, homothetic fiber family or differentiable critical cap
is assumed. Assumption (A) is stronger than bare pure-base binding: a
minimal atomic halfspace through an interior point of B may be much
lighter than B, and that case is not covered by (1).

## 2. Deepest midpoints and the face/parity count

The buffered superlevel region at fixed Q is convex in the full real
base-continuous space. Explicitly, its nonvertical constraints have the
form

    a.z+u.X-epsilon f_ell(z,X) Gamma(u)<=c_Q(a,u),

where c_Q is the right upper quantile of the ACTUAL mixed measure,
f_ell=(ell E/M)^(1/(d+1)) is jointly concave on the canonical fiber hull,
and Gamma is fixed for this body. The pure-base constraints are ordinary
convex halfspace constraints. Thus if (p,y_p) and (q,y_q) are actual
buffered maximizing points and their midpoint base m is in Lambda, the
midpoint mark belongs to the actual fiber K_m by compatibility and has
depth at least Q. Global maximality makes it a maximizing mark. Therefore

    p,q in I of the same parity => (p+q)/2 in I.                (3)

Since Q<M by (2), all these minimal faces are proper. All distinct
faces in the list {F_p:p in I} have mass Q by (1). They are
an antichain: a strict inclusion of two faces includes an additional
vertex of B in the larger one, hence an additional point of P with
positive mass. Choose one deepest witness p_i in the relative interior
of each distinct face F_i, i=1,...,s.

The minimal face of a strict midpoint of two points in B is the join of
their minimal faces. Indeed any face containing the midpoint contains
both endpoints, and the smallest face containing both endpoints is their
face join. If p_i and p_j for distinct faces had the same parity, (3)
would make their midpoint deepest. Its minimal face F_i join F_j strictly
contains F_i because of the antichain property. Its mass would be greater
than Q, contrary to (1) applied to that midpoint. Hence the witnesses
have pairwise distinct occupied parities, and

    s<=k.                                                     (4)

No claim is made that ALL points outside these faces use different
parities from points inside them.

Let

    U=P intersect (union_(i=1)^s F_i),       M_U=sum_(z in U)V_z.

Overlaps are counted only once. From (1), (2) and (4),

    M_U<=sum_i V(F_i)=s Q<=k Q<Gamma_d M<M.                     (5)

In particular U is a PROPER subset of P. No generic disjointness or
lower-dimensional-contact assumption is used.

## 3. Coherent affine interior centers on all overlapping simplex faces

Choose one point c_v in int K_v for every vertex v of B occurring in
some F_i. On each simplex F_i, let c_i(z) be the unique affine map taking
these chosen values at its vertices. For every z in F_i, barycentric
compatibility puts c_i(z) in int K_z: each chosen c_v has an interior
ball, and the corresponding Minkowski combination retains a positive
ball about its convex combination, including on subfaces.

For any two F_i,F_j, their nonempty intersection is a common face of
both simplices. Its vertices are precisely their common vertices. The
two affine maps agree on those vertices and therefore on their entire
intersection. We obtain a SINGLE well-defined center c_z for every
z in U, affine on each F_i. It need not extend to one affine map on B.

Fix 0<t<1 and define the ACTUAL new fibers

    K_z(t)=c_z+(1-t)(K_z-c_z)  if z in U,
    K_z(t)=K_z                if z outside U.                  (6)

This family is exactly compatible. If the target q of an anchored
representation lies outside U, every modified input fiber is a subset
of its old fiber and the target is unchanged. If q lies in U, choose
any F_i containing q. Since F_i is a face, EVERY positive-coefficient
input base in ANY anchored representation of q lies in F_i. All these
inputs are modified by the same factor about the affine centers c_i.
Therefore

    sum_j lambda_j K_(z_j)(t)
       =c_i(q)+(1-t)[sum_j lambda_j K_(z_j)-c_i(q)]
       subset c_i(q)+(1-t)[K_q-c_i(q)]=K_q(t).                  (7)

If q belongs to several selected faces, the centers already agree and
(7) defines the same target body. This proves simultaneous compatibility
across all overlaps, not only within disjoint face components.

All fibers stay positive and converge in Hausdorff distance. Their
canonical convex hull has exactly these sampled fibers. A deficient
base rank may be repaired by the established rational perpendicular
thickening without changing sampled fibers.

The same construction works for nonsimplex faces if coherent affine
interior center maps on those faces are supplied as an explicit premise.
Their existence is NOT presumed for an arbitrary convex projection.

## 4. Actual global buffered descent with updated normalizations

Put r=(1-t)^d. Every volume in U is multiplied by r, so

    M(t)=M-M_U(1-r),       V(F_i;t)=r Q.                        (8)

Each proper face F_i is exposed. A closed pure-base halfspace with trace
P intersect F_i contains every marked point over that face. It bounds
that entire fiber subfamily's buffered depth by rQ, independent of the
new energy, covariance, multiplier, and continuous source point.
All old maximizing bases are in U. The finitely many bases outside U
have a strict old maximum gap. The positive-fiber all-direction buffered
continuity theorem preserves that gap for small t, while rQ tends to Q.

For precision, let the multiplier change by only the scalar

    ell_t(z)=c(t) ell(z),
    c(t)=exp[-sum_z V_z(t) log ell(z)/M(t)].                    (9)

It is positive affine, has the required updated weighted geometric mean
one, and c(0)=1. The actual M(t), within-fiber covariance Sigma(t), and
energy are all recomputed. They depend continuously on the positive
Hausdorff path, so the continuity statement applies to this invariant
buffer rather than to a frozen normalization.

It follows that the ACTUAL global maximum Q(t) satisfies Q(t)<=rQ for
all sufficiently small t>0. By (5) and (8),

    Q(t)/M(t) <=rQ/[M-M_U(1-r)] <Q/M.                          (10)

The strict inequality is exactly (1-r)(M-M_U)>0. Thus this is a genuine
unpenalized descent, with no assumed deepest-source path, differential
cap allocation, or first-order approximation. This proves the theorem.

The proof is not valid after adding a penalty unless that penalty's
actual derivative or finite change is also accounted for. In particular
no penalty is silently held fixed in (10).

## 5. Exact obstruction to replacing exposed faces by closed minors

Use the actual three-interval family K_-1=K_0=K_1=[-1,1], with the positive
geometric-mean affine multiplier from
`candidate 5f79e6103cd27dac`,
Section 2. For every prescribed small epsilon>0 this gives a genuine
buffered raw maximum Q=4 at the middle base, pure-base depth 4 there,
and total M=6. All proper closed-minor quotas are strict. The normalized
depth 2/3 is SAFE; this is not a bad-minimum counterexample.

The two minimal atomic caps at the middle source have traces

    T_+={0,1},       T_-={-1,0}.

Both are proper closed minors, but neither is a face of conv(P). Try to
shrink the fibers in T_+ by a common homothety factor r in (0,1), leaving
K_-1 unchanged. Even allowing arbitrary translated centers, the new
middle and right intervals have lengths 2r. Their necessary midpoint
inclusion would require

    (length K_-1 + length K_1(t))/2 <=length K_0(t),
    1+r<=2r,

which is false for every r<1. Thus no choice of centers repairs this
closed-subfamily contraction. The same obstruction holds for T_-.
Shrinking their union means shrinking ALL three fibers, whose invariant
normalized buffered depth is unchanged by the common homothety.

This is an actual anchored-contact obstruction, not a graph analogy.
Closedness ensures convex combinations of points OF the minor remain
inside it; it does not ensure every anchored representation TARGETING
it uses only its points. The latter is exactly the face property used
in (7). Assumption (1), or a different mechanism controlling these
incoming anchored contacts, is therefore material.

## 6. What this excludes and what remains open

For a rank-two base, every nonempty proper face is an edge or a vertex,
hence a simplex. The theorem therefore excludes an unpenalized bad
minimum whenever every maximizing base is paid atomically by the mass
of its own boundary edge or vertex. These bases may be nonvertices and
may share edges or lie on intersecting selected faces.

The theorem does not cover a maximizing base in the relative interior
of the full base polytope, whose minimal face has mass M while its atomic
depth can be much smaller. It also does not cover a mixed menu containing
proper continuous caps and atomic groups unless all its old maximizing
fibers receive an actual covering bound under the same deformation.
Those branches retain their original contact and selection constraints.
